title: Portraits Through Time
description: Faces that have held our gaze across the centuries.

items.title: Miniature Vessel in the Form of a Portrait Head with Painted Cheeks
items.description_narrative: This ceramic vessel, crafted by the ancient Moche culture, vividly depicts a human head adorned with painted cheeks. Its miniature scale and intricate pigment details suggest a specialized function, perhaps for ritual or offering, showcasing Moche mastery in sculptural pottery.
items.tags: moche, pre-columbian, ceramic, portrait, head, vessel, ancient andes, ritual

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.description_narrative: This self-portrait by Walter Shirlaw offers a direct gaze, capturing the artist's likeness with a palpable sense of his presence. Created in 1878 using oil on canvas, the work exemplifies his personal engagement with portraiture.
items.tags: self-portrait, portraiture, oil painting, 19th century, american art, realism, figurative, introspective

items.title: Untitled (Painted Portrait of Charles Coit)
items.description_narrative: This untitled daguerreotype captures a painted portrait of Charles Coit, a testament to the early photographic processes of the mid-19th century. Created in 1855 or 1856, this detailed image offers a glimpse into historical portraiture through an innovative medium.
items.tags: portrait, photography, daguerreotype, 19th century, historical, formal, man

items.title: Untitled (Portrait of a Man Painting)
items.description_narrative: This ambrotype captures a man in the act of painting, offering a glimpse into artistic practice in the mid-19th century. The unique photographic process renders a positive image on glass, creating a distinctive visual quality.
items.tags: portrait, photography, 19th century, ambrotype, artist, painting, man

items.title: Portrait of an Artist
items.description_narrative: This 1644 oil on canvas depicts an artist, likely a self-portrait or a fellow painter, captured with a direct gaze. The work, attributed to a follower of Frans Hals, reflects the spirited brushwork and psychological depth characteristic of Dutch Golden Age portraiture.
items.tags: portrait, 17th century, dutch golden age, baroque, oil painting, male figure, artist portrait

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.medium: Oil on artist's board, mounted on cradled panel
items.description_narrative: This striking self-portrait by Vincent van Gogh, painted in 1887, captures the artist with an intense gaze. Executed in oil on artist's board, it exemplifies his distinctive Post-Impressionist brushwork and vibrant palette.
items.tags: self-portrait, oil painting, vincent van gogh, post-impressionism, dutch art, 19th century, portraiture, vivid

items.title: The Captive Slave (Ira Aldridge)
items.description_narrative: John Philip Simpson's 1827 oil painting, "The Captive Slave (Ira Aldridge)," powerfully depicts the celebrated African American actor Ira Aldridge. This dramatic work, featuring Aldridge in a poignant portrayal, aligns with the burgeoning abolitionist movements of the early 19th century.
items.tags: ira aldridge, portrait, abolition, slavery, romanticism, 19th century, dramatic, british art

items.title: Portrait of a Man with Gray Hair
items.description_narrative: This striking oil on canvas portrays a man with gray hair, captured with directness and psychological insight by Sir Henry Raeburn. The artist's distinctive style emphasizes the sitter's character through a masterful command of light and shadow.
items.tags: portrait, man, oil painting, Scottish art, 19th century, realism

items.title: Édouard Manet
items.description_narrative: Henri Fantin-Latour's 1867 oil on canvas depicts his contemporary and friend, Édouard Manet. This formal portrait captures Manet in a contemplative pose, offering insight into their artistic circle in 19th-century Paris.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, manet, fantin-latour, 19th century, french art, realism, formal

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.medium: Etching and engraving in black on ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: This self-portrait by Cornelis Visscher, created using the detailed techniques of etching and engraving, captures the artist's likeness with precision. Visscher was a notable printmaker during the Dutch Golden Age.
items.tags: self-portrait, etching, engraving, dutch golden age, printmaking, 17th century, master engraver

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.description_narrative: This intimate self-portrait by Frédéric Bazille captures the artist in a reflective moment. Painted with oil on canvas between 1865 and 1866, it offers a direct gaze from the young painter to the viewer.
items.tags: self-portrait, portrait, oil painting, male figure, 19th century, french art, realism

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.medium: Etching in black on ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: This striking self-portrait by Edgar Degas captures the artist in his youth, rendered with an intense gaze. Executed in 1857 as an etching, it showcases his early mastery of printmaking techniques.
items.tags: self-portrait, etching, printmaking, 19th century, french art, early work, degas

items.title: Self-Portrait in a Fur Cap
items.medium: Monochrome pastel (grisaille) on blue-gray laid paper
items.description_narrative: Joseph Wright of Derby presents himself in a monochrome pastel self-portrait, rendered in grisaille on blue-gray laid paper. This work showcases the artist's skill in capturing form and light through a restricted palette.
items.tags: self-portrait, pastel, monochrome, grisaille, 18th century, british art, enlightenment, portraiture

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.description_narrative: This self-portrait captures Nicolas de Largillière, a prominent French painter, at work. Painted with oil on canvas, it offers a glimpse into the artist's identity and his craft during the early 18th century.
items.tags: self-portrait, portraiture, oil painting, Baroque, Rococo, 18th century, French art, artist

items.title: Self-Portrait Etching at a Window
items.medium: Etching, drypoint and burin in black on ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: Rembrandt van Rijn captures his own likeness in this poignant 1648 etching, depicting himself at a window. Through the interplay of light and shadow, the artist reveals a contemplative gaze, masterfully rendered with drypoint and burin.
items.tags: self-portrait, etching, drypoint, burin, dutch golden age, rembrandt, introspection, printmaking

items.title: Self-Portrait with a Visor
items.medium: Pastel on blue laid paper, laid down on canvas
items.description_narrative: Jean Siméon Chardin captures his own likeness in 'Self-Portrait with a Visor,' executed in pastel on blue laid paper around 1776. This work presents the artist in a domestic setting, wearing a visor, with a direct and contemplative gaze.
items.tags: self-portrait, portraiture, pastel, rococo, 18th century, french art, contemplative, domestic

items.title: Portrait of a Woman
items.description_narrative: This etching on paper depicts a portrait of a woman. Through the intricate lines of the printmaking technique, the artist captures her likeness with detail.
items.tags: etching, portrait, woman, print, figure, graphic art

items.title: Portrait of a Woman
items.description_narrative: Amedeo Modigliani's 'Portrait of a Woman' embodies his distinctive approach to portraiture, characterized by an elongated figure and a subtly expressive, mask-like face. Painted with oil on cardboard around 1917-1919, this artwork reflects the artist's unique modernist vision.
items.tags: portrait, woman, modigliani, modernist, elongated, oil painting, figure

items.title: Portrait of a Woman
items.description_narrative: Jean Léon Gérôme's 'Portrait of a Woman,' painted in oil on canvas in 1851, captures a solitary female figure with meticulous detail. The work exemplifies Gérôme's early mastery of academic realism and portraiture.
items.tags: portrait, woman, 19th century, oil painting, academic realism, french art

items.title: Portrait of a Woman
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas painting, titled 'Portrait of a Woman', was created by John Wollaston between 1749 and 1752. It exemplifies the common practice of portraiture during the mid-18th century.
items.tags: portraiture, 18th century, colonial american, oil painting, woman, formal, realism
